solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tell fib about retired supermodel being flexible

indicators.note: to retire is to go back or withdraw, so the letters are read backwards
about means around, so one piece is placed round the outside of another

blocks.note: to tell a fib is to lie
Kate Moss, the famous British supermodel

explanation.surface: Someone lying about the age or fitness of a retired supermodel, apparently still supple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reads like a description of the model, but it is the instruction to reverse; Kate Moss is the go-to supermodel in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes a body that is supple and graceful, bending easily, which is what flexible means.

clue.text: Act violently, like husband punching ruffian

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so these letters are pushed inside another word

blocks.note: like and as are interchangeable in comparisons
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
a lout is a rough, uncouth man

explanation.surface: A violent scene in which a husband hits a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like husband' joins into one piece before going inside; 'punching' looks like the violence but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is a phrasal verb meaning to strike or attack suddenly and wildly, in words or blows.

clue.text: Traitor taking harnesses off

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or bad, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A disloyal stable hand removing the horses' tack.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'taking harnesses' rearrange into the four-word phrase; 'off' reads as part of 'taking off' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake in the grass is an idiom for a treacherous person who pretends to be a friend while secretly betraying you.

clue.text: Kiln starts to overheat after setting temperature

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only first letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
T is the usual abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Warning that a kiln will overheat once the temperature has been set.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of three consecutive words, then T. An oast is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent's countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln, specifically one used for drying hops before brewing, and a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Exclusive English literature topped list

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its top, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lit is the short form of literature
taken as written before losing its head

explanation.surface: An English literature title that topped the bestseller list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped list' looks like a book heading the charts, but it means LIST with its top letter cut off, leaving IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elitist favours a select few and keeps others out, which is what exclusive means as an adjective.

clue.text: Cure-all somewhat cheap, an ace alternative

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring spaces and punctuation

explanation.surface: A cheap cure-all touted as a fine alternative remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside chea-P AN ACE A-lternative.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for every illness or problem, which is exactly a cure-all.

clue.text: Stupid boy allowed crumpet

blocks.note: Private Pike in the BBC sitcom Dad's Army is forever called 'you stupid boy' by Captain Mainwaring
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A foolish lad permitted a crumpet, or a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British wartime comedy; 'You stupid boy!' is Mainwaring's catchphrase to young Pike. Crumpet is also British slang for attractive people, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a regional British and Australian name for a thin, flat crumpet or griddle cake.

clue.text: Element of Tube lighting?

blocks.note: surface reading: a part of the lighting system on the London Underground
setter's reading: the chemical element that glows in gas-filled tube lights

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T points to the London Underground, known as the Tube; read lower-case, it is a glass tube filled with a glowing gas.
explanation.definitionFit: This noble gas is a chemical element, and it fills the glass tubes of bright advertising signs.

clue.text: IKEA makes these amazingly shrewd forecasts

indicators.note: something done amazingly is done in a startling, unexpected way, so the letters land in a surprising order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Praise for a furniture company's sharp business predictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: IKEA, the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain, sells these among many other things.
explanation.definitionFit: These bedroom storage units with sliding compartments are a typical product of the flat-pack furniture retailer.

clue.text: Very bad baby’s ma lost bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the answer is held within these words

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring the apostrophe and spaces

explanation.surface: A mother so careless she has lost her baby's bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like a noun, the feeding bottles, but works as a verb: b-ABY'S MA L-ost holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means extremely poor or appalling, as deep as an abyss, so it is a strong word for very bad.

clue.text: Cyclists make pod cast – chaotically funny scenes!

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould, so the letters are thrown into a new shape

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Cyclists record a podcast full of hilarious mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pod cast' reads as the single word podcast, hiding that 'cast' is the anagram signal for the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick comedy is boisterous physical humour built on pratfalls and collisions, so its scenes are chaotic and funny.

clue.text: 3 witches in a gathering failing at the outset

definitions.note: a cross-reference: the answer to 3 down, OAST, is a kiln

indicators.note: failing at the start means the first part is missing, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: a coven is an assembly of witches

explanation.surface: A gathering of three witches that falls apart at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer of 3 down, a kiln; the number also makes the surface read as three witches, as in Macbeth. COVEN loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a type of oven, a heated chamber for baking or drying, so one can stand for the other.

clue.text: Trouble occupying very advanced, superior house

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within others

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
ill as a noun means harm or trouble
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: Problems taking over a very upmarket, modern home.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL sits between V and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large, grand residence, often detached and in its own grounds, so a superior house.

clue.text: First half of the alphabet, something very small

blocks.note: first meaning: the letters running from the first to the thirteenth, written as a phrase
second meaning: a tiny particle

explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the alphabet runs 'A to M', which written as one word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element, so it is the standard image of a minute thing.

clue.text: Shuttle service runs aboard iron railway

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be inside a vessel, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A shuttle that runs on an iron railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: The runs go aboard the iron and railway joined together, landing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a boat making regular short trips back and forth, so it provides a shuttle service.

clue.text: Fear doctor each day

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ea is the abbreviation for each
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A patient who is afraid of seeing the doctor every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Three standard abbreviations in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great apprehension or terror about something to come, a close synonym of fear.

clue.text: Line that touches bronzed chap?

blocks.note: a bronzed person has a tan
a gent is a man, a chap

explanation.surface: A chat-up line that moves a suntanned man.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: a 'tan gent' is a bronzed chap.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line meeting a curve at exactly one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Our Tim goes out, ending in awful commotion

indicators.note: going out of order or out of line means losing the set arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as material to rearrange
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A family's Tim leaves the house, ending in a dreadful row.
explanation.walkthrough: The six letters of 'Our Tim' plus the L that ends 'awful' are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance and confusion, so commotion is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Connery’s lost somewhere to rest his butt

indicators.note: the actor Sean Connery is famous for slurring S into SH, so the word is as he would pronounce it

blocks.note: lost means astray, which comes out with a slushy S in that famous Scottish voice

explanation.surface: Sean Connery has lost a place to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTRAY in Connery's distinctive lisping accent becomes ASH-TRAY. 'Butt' looks like his backside but is a cigarette end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is a dish where a smoker stubs out or rests a cigarette end, and a butt is that stub.

clue.text: Hancock regularly employed individual in dock

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, so only alternate ones are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A man named Hancock who often gave work to someone later on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of hAnCoCk gives ACC. The dock is the enclosure in a courtroom where the defendant stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused is the defendant charged with a crime, who stands in the courtroom dock during a trial.

clue.text: Bad behaviour by boy running around Exeter’s walls

indicators.note: walls are the outside edges of a place, so only the outer letters are kept
running around something circles it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a yob is a loutish youth; the word began as backslang for boy
taken as written
the first and last letters of the city's name

explanation.surface: A lad tearing round the old Roman city walls of Exeter, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' does double duty in the surface but is fodder here, wrapped round the city's walls. Yob is British slang for a hooligan, and Exeter is a walled cathedral city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbery is British slang for the loutish, antisocial conduct of hooligans, so it means bad behaviour.

clue.text: Leave a group of musicians working

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group of musicians
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Quitting a band that is still gigging.
explanation.walkthrough: A + BAND + ON read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone or something is to desert or forsake it, which is to leave it behind.

clue.text: Outstanding art gallery film material

blocks.note: ace means excellent, outstanding
the Tate is a group of major British art galleries, such as Tate Modern in London

explanation.surface: A superb gallery showing film or video works.
explanation.walkthrough: ACE then TATE; the Tate is the famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose acetate is the plastic used as the base for photographic film and overhead transparencies.

clue.text: Close cup game that goes on fairly late

blocks.note: nigh means near or close
in British football, a cup tie is a knockout match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A tight cup match that runs on late into the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on' suggests a match running into extra time, but here it means is put on, as clothing is.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment put on at bedtime, so it is worn late in the evening.

clue.text: Convict’s first time in prison

indicators.note: first points to the opening position, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A convict serving their first stretch behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus AGE. 'First time in prison' reads as one phrase, but 'first' belongs to 'Convict's' and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is an enclosure of bars for confining a captive, so it can stand for any prison or jail.

clue.text: Convent always storing odd bits of Bible

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another
the odd-numbered positions are the first, third and fifth, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: ay (also aye) is an old word for always or ever
the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A nunnery that has always kept scraps of an old Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Ay is a poetic or dialect word for always, rarely met outside verse and crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a building occupied by a community of monks or nuns, so it can be a convent.

clue.text: Sudden twinge leads to Annie needing to have PG Tips

indicators.note: leading letters are the ones at the front, so only first letters are kept
to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds another
tips are the extreme ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: the two end letters of these initials
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Annie gets a sharp twinge that only a cup of tea will fix.
explanation.walkthrough: PG Tips is a popular British tea brand; its 'tips' are P and G, which hold AN. 'Leads to Annie' wants to give A alone, but the leading letters run on into 'needing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pang is a sudden sharp spasm of pain or emotion, so it is a sudden twinge.

clue.text: Kent port trade

blocks.note: first meaning: a seaside town on the coast of Kent, a county in south-east England
second meaning: to buy and sell, do business

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like the commerce of a Kentish harbour; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a coastal settlement in south-east England, and as a verb the word means to do business in goods.

clue.text: This compiler’s hosting extremely talkative couple

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece is held inside another
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I, and 'compiler's' here is 'compiler is', so I'M
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: The setter is entertaining a pair who never stop chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This compiler's' means 'I am', so I'M, which holds TE.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informal for two people in a romantic relationship, as in 'they are an item', so a couple.

clue.text: Branch of US Govt affirmed European role meant ignoring America

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to affirm is to state
E is the abbreviation for European
an actor's role is their part
taken as written before losing a letter
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A US government department confirming that a European's role excluded America.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANT without its A becomes MENT, ending the long charade STATED-E-PART-MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American federal department handling foreign affairs, headed by the Secretary of State.

clue.text: Show with cops and drama

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A television police drama series.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the British rank of Detective Inspector, so several cops are DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to exhibit it or put it on view, which is what show means as a verb or noun.

clue.text: Postgrads spotted cycling in enormous numbers

indicators.note: a cycle goes round, so letters from one end are carried round to the other

blocks.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts, a postgraduate degree
spotted means seen

explanation.surface: Graduate students seen out riding bikes in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: After joining the two pieces, the last two letters cycle round to the front. 'Cycling' suggests bikes, but it is the rotation signal.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is a French borrowing meaning all together as a group, so in a great crowd.
